findings.issue_text: **`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168`** — `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the *raw* input `guests`, not the filtered `uniqueGuests`. If a submitted email is a duplicate of an existing attendee (and thus filtered out of the DB write), that existing attendee will still match `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in `email-manager.ts` and incorrectly receive a full "new guest" `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the lighter `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`.

**`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:64-67`** — Blacklist bypass via casing: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased, but `guest` (the raw submitted email) is compared as-is (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), and the duplicate check (`guest === attendee.email`) is also case-sensitive. An email like `Test@Blacklisted.com` bypasses the blacklist, and `Test@example.com` vs `test@example.com` could create duplicate attendee rows for the same person.

**`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52-59`** — `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` throws Prisma's internal `NotFoundError` (not a clean `TRPCError`) if `booking.userId` is null — this surfaces as an unhandled 500 rather than a friendly error, and it's also a redundant query since `booking.user` was already fetched with `include` in the initial `findFirst`.

No check on `booking.status` before allowing guest additions — guests can seemingly be added to a `CANCELLED` or `REJECTED` booking, which would send confusing "you've been added to this event" emails for an event that isn't happening.

No check for `eventType.disableGuests` (or equivalent event-type-level policy) before allowing this mutation, which would let this endpoint bypass an organizer's explicit configuration disallowing extra guests on that event type.

**`apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json`** — the error message key `you_do_not_have_permission` used in the `FORBIDDEN` throw (`addGuests.handler.ts:48`) is never added to the locale file, so the toast in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:34` (`t(err.message)`) will render the raw untranslated key instead of a user-facing string.

No automated tests were added (no unit test for `addGuestsHandler`'s authorization/dedup/blacklist logic, no component/e2e test for `AddGuestsDialog`). Given this touches auth, calendar sync, and email delivery, some coverage — at least for the permission matrix and dedup/blacklist filtering — is warranted before merge.

**`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165-169`** — `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs *after* the DB attendee rows are already persisted, with no wrapping try/catch and no rollback. If the calendar sync fails, the request errors out but the guests remain persisted in the DB — an inconsistent, silently-partial state the user isn't informed about (they'd only see a generic error toast and might retry, adding guests twice).

**`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:171-174`** — email send failures are `console.log`'d rather than logged through the project's structured logger, and the error itself is discarded, making failures hard to diagnose in production.

There is no upper bound on the number of guests that can be added in one call; combined with the missing test coverage, this leaves room for abuse (mass-adding attendees to spam their inboxes with calendar invites).

Silent dropping of blacklisted/duplicate emails: the caller has no way to know which of their submitted emails were filtered out vs. actually added (`{ message: "Guests added" }` doesn't report this), which could look like a bug from the UI end when someone expects N guests added but fewer show up.

`packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:22` — using array `index` as the React `key` for a removable/reorderable list is a minor anti-pattern that can cause subtle focus/state issues if the list ever grows more complex; low risk currently since inputs are fully controlled.
`apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:16` — `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (a zod schema) is recreated on every render instead of being hoisted outside the component; trivial perf nit.
Only `en/common.json` received new locale strings; other locale files are untouched (likely fine if translations are backfilled by an external pipeline, but worth confirming project convention).

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52-59`** — `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` throws Prisma's internal `NotFoundError` (not a clean `TRPCError`) if `booking.userId` is null — this surfaces as an unhandled 500 rather than a friendly error, and it's also a redundant query since `booking.user` was already fetched with `include` in the initial `findFirst`.

adjudication.rationale: The handler explicitly treats `booking.userId` as possibly falsy by using `booking.userId || 0`, and then calls `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow` with that value. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined`, this becomes `id: 0`, which will not match any user and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma "not found" error (not a `TRPCError`). There is no surrounding try/catch converting it to a `TRPCError`, so it will propagate as an internal error. Additionally, the initial `prisma.booking.findFirst` already includes `user` (with related destinationCalendar/credentials), so querying the organizer again is redundant and could have used `booking.user` directly (or thrown a clean `TRPCError` if missing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check on `booking.status` before allowing guest additions — guests can seemingly be added to a `CANCELLED` or `REJECTED` booking, which would send confusing "you've been added to this event" emails for an event that isn't happening.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation/handler does not check any booking lifecycle state before updating attendees and sending emails. In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched by `id` only (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })`) and then attendees are added via `prisma.booking.update(...)`, followed by `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. There is no guard against cancelled/rejected bookings (no `booking.status` check or filter), and the UI adds an always-available action (`add_members`) in `BookingListItem.tsx` without any status gating. So, if cancelled/rejected bookings are present in the list and have a `status` field (as is typical in this codebase), this diff allows adding guests and triggers “Guests added” emails for bookings that may no longer be happening.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check for `eventType.disableGuests` (or equivalent event-type-level policy) before allowing this mutation, which would let this endpoint bypass an organizer's explicit configuration disallowing extra guests on that event type.

adjudication.rationale: In the added `addGuestsHandler`, the booking’s `eventType` is loaded but no event-type-level “disable guests” flag is referenced or checked. However, the diff does not show that an `eventType.disableGuests` (or any equivalent policy field) actually exists in the schema/types, nor does it show any existing guests-policy enforcement elsewhere that this endpoint is now bypassing. As written, the finding relies on an assumed configuration option that is not verifiable from the diff alone, so it’s speculative rather than a concrete defect proven by the changes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `addGuests.handler.ts` throwing `new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "you_do_not_have_permission" })` and `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` calling `t(err.message)` on error. However, the diff does not show the full contents of `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json`, only newly added keys; it does not prove that `you_do_not_have_permission` is missing. That key could already exist in the locale file prior to this change, so the claim “never added” is not verifiable from the diff alone.

Given this touches auth, calendar sync, and email delivery, some coverage — at least for the permission matrix and dedup/blacklist filtering — is warranted before merge.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new behavior (new TRPC mutation `viewer.bookings.addGuests`, `addGuestsHandler` with auth/blacklist/dedup logic, a new `AddGuestsDialog` UI flow, and new email sending logic), but there are no additions or changes to any test files (unit/integration/component/e2e). This makes the finding factually verifiable from the diff: no automated coverage was added for the new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165-169`** — `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs *after* the DB attendee rows are already persisted, with no wrapping try/catch and no rollback. If the calendar sync fails, the request errors out but the guests remain persisted in the DB — an inconsistent, silently-partial state the user isn't informed about (they'd only see a generic error toast and might retry, adding guests twice).

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code persists new attendee rows via prisma.booking.update(...createMany...) before calling `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. That calendar update is not wrapped in try/catch (only the subsequent email sending is), and there is no DB transaction/rollback. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the TRPC mutation will error out while the DB changes have already been committed, and the client’s `onSuccess` invalidation won’t run—leaving the UI stale even though guests were added. The proposed “might retry adding guests twice” part is less solid because a retry will re-fetch attendees and the handler filters out existing emails, but the partial/inconsistent state on failure is real and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:171-174`** — email send failures are `console.log`'d rather than logged through the project's structured logger, and the error itself is discarded, making failures hard to diagnose in production.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the `sendAddGuestsEmails` call is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not include the caught `err` (nor uses any structured/project logger). This discards the actual error details and makes production diagnosis harder; the behavior is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: There is no upper bound on the number of guests that can be added in one call; combined with the missing test coverage, this leaves room for abuse (mass-adding attendees to spam their inboxes with calendar invites).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `addGuests` mutation whose input schema (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema`) allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` or other upper bound, and the UI (`MultiEmail`) allows adding arbitrary additional email fields. The handler then `createMany` inserts all provided guests and calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which triggers outbound emails/ICS updates for attendees. This makes it verifiably possible to submit a very large guest list in a single call and cause mass email sends (spam/abuse risk). However, the claim about “missing test coverage” is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent dropping of blacklisted/duplicate emails: the caller has no way to know which of their submitted emails were filtered out vs. actually added (`{ message: "Guests added" }` doesn't report this), which could look like a bug from the UI end when someone expects N guests added but fewer show up.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server filters the submitted `guests` into `uniqueGuests` by removing emails already in `booking.attendees` and any `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, then only creates attendees for `uniqueGuests`. However, the mutation response is always `return { message: "Guests added" };` (no list/count of actually-added emails), and it does not surface which inputs were ignored. This can lead to the UI/user thinking all submitted emails were added when fewer were actually persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:22` — using array `index` as the React `key` for a removable/reorderable list is a minor anti-pattern that can cause subtle focus/state issues if the list ever grows more complex; low risk currently since inputs are fully controlled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the component renders a dynamic list of email inputs with `value.map((field, index) => (<li key={index}> ...))` and also supports removing items via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. Using the array index as the React key in a list where items can be removed causes keys for subsequent items to change, so React may reuse the wrong component/DOM instance for the next item. Even with controlled `value`, this can still produce subtle UX/correctness issues (e.g., focus/cursor jumping, any internal state inside `EmailField` being associated with the wrong row). This behavior is directly implied by the diff, so the finding is verifiable and not just stylistic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:16` — `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (a zod schema) is recreated on every render instead of being hoisted outside the component; trivial perf nit.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog the zod schema is indeed defined inside the component (`const ZAddGuestsInputSchema = ...`), so it will be recreated on each render. However, this is a minor micro-optimization/style/perf nit and not a clear bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Only `en/common.json` received new locale strings; other locale files are untouched (likely fine if translations are backfilled by an external pipeline, but worth confirming project convention).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show new translation keys added only to `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json`. However, whether this is a problem is not verifiable from the diff alone: many i18n setups allow missing keys in other locales (fallback to `en` or to the key string), and the finding itself frames it as “likely fine” and “worth confirming” rather than a concrete defect. There’s no demonstrated runtime breakage or failing build shown in the change.
